name: Indian Oil Marketing (IOC/BPCL/HPCL)
summary: Indian OMCs, Day 241. Pump prices stay frozen while the Indian basket runs ~$120 and ICRA puts the diesel under-recovery at ~₹20/L; there is no excise relief or compensation, only a diesel export-levy cut (16 Oct). Yet IOC, BPCL and HPCL rose 1–4% while crude rose 10%, because the RBI's dollar window removes their currency risk and the market prices eventual government support. That policy put is the exposure: if the window narrows before Brent falls, OMC equities reprice.

recent_signals.headline: Pump prices frozen (Delhi diesel ₹95.20, petrol ₹102.12) with a ~₹20/l diesel under-recovery (ICRA, 25 Oct). IOC Q2 FY27 standalone profit ₹21,630 cr (30 Oct) on 'a temporary decline in crude oil prices from mid-June to mid-August', petchem/gas margins and LPG compensation — and warned 'profitability in upcoming quarters may be adversely impacted by inventory losses'; HPCL carries an unrecognised ₹18,049 cr negative LPG buffer. Private refiners win: Reliance O2C EBITDA +68% on 'exceptional refining cracks' (30 Oct, after the close). Diesel export levy raised to ₹11.5/l (31 Oct) keeps product at home. **NON-MOVER: OMC EQUITIES ROSE WITH CRUDE.** IOC +3.7%, BPCL +1.0%, HPCL +4.4% since 13 Oct while Brent rose 10% and ICRA puts the diesel under-recovery at ~₹20/L (doubled). Pump prices frozen with the Indian basket ~$120 (BS: 15-year high average); diesel export levy cut to ₹8.50 (16 Oct); no excise relief, no OMC compensation announced, LPG unchanged. The RBI's dollar window removes OMC currency risk — a policy put the market is pricing. (CONFIRMED prices; REPORTED under-recovery; markets C9, intel IND-A11)

**OMCs: pump prices frozen with the basket $116–121; under-recoveries ~₹5/l petrol, ~₹23/l diesel (BusinessToday 23 Sep, unnamed govt source — REPORTED); commercial LPG +₹62.50 to ₹2,810 (1 Oct); domestic LPG unchanged ₹942.** Export windfall levies cut from 1 Oct (diesel ₹20→₹16/l; ATF ₹15→₹10.5/l). **State support moved to the currency: RBI's 10-Oct window meets IOC/BPCL/HPCL's entire daily dollar needs from reserves** — removes OMC dollar buying from the market. Sourcing (Kpler, Sept): imports ~5.3 mb/d; Russia 1.74 mb/d (lowest since April; ~35% share vs ~56% July); Iraq 575 kb/d, Saudi 566 kb/d (+63%), UAE 480 kb/d, US 141 kb/d; no Iranian crude. IOC ₹126.14 / BPCL ₹287.4 / HPCL ₹329.0 (13 Oct; flat-to-down since 7 Oct). — mixed tags.

**No OMC pricing action or government freeze instruction surfaced 17–21 Sep; Brent −7.7% to $100.34 eases the under-recovery arithmetic at the margin; US retail diesel a record $6.31 shows product cracks lag crude.** — negative finding.

**One-day crack relief: heating oil −5.0% / RBOB −6.8% on 16 Sep (restart guidance + EIA builds) trims the OMC margin squeeze at the margin — but Brent >$100 for six settles, INR 96 and diesel scarcity (EIA: distillate <100mb this month) keep under-recoveries live. No pump-price change found. Autos −2% Tue on the fuel read-through. (yfinance; EIA; HDFC Sky) — CONFIRMED prices.**

OMCs (IOC/BPCL/HPCL) back in the margin squeeze: Brent $107 (+23% 1M) with no visible pump-price pass-through found this sweep; the Iranian-crude discount channel ($3–4/bbl offers) is dead with the waiver; the RBI OMC credit-facility wind-down trigger is off the table. Diesel is the crisis product globally (US record $6.05–6.20; heating oil +48% 3M) — India's diesel-heavy demand mix is the exposure. (markets.md; Mint — CONFIRMED prices; pass-through NOT FOUND)

**NO FIFTH HIKE — THE PASS-THROUGH PAUSED AFTER FOUR HIKES; THE MAY 25 FOURTH HIKE STANDS AND DELHI PETROL HAS NOW CROSSED ₹100 TO ₹102.12.** Over the ~48h window (no brief May 26) there was no new OMC price action: the cumulative ~₹7.5/L since May 15 (May 15 +₹3; May 19 +~90p; May 23 +~87-91p; May 25 +₹2.61-2.71, the largest) remains the operative total. The May 25 hike fully propagated city-by-city — **Delhi petrol crossed ₹100 to ₹102.12 (diesel ₹95.20)**, Mumbai petrol ₹111.21 (Goodreturns, India.com, BusinessToday May 27). **The trigger stays `active_fired` but is NOT firing harder** — no new action this window; the pause is itself the signal. A plateau after four hikes is consistent with the cadence having broken to economics-led on May 25 and OMCs having recovered enough of the under-recovery envelope for now. **The oil backdrop eased marginally but stays out-of-range**: operative Brent rebounded to ~$99 (CNBC: Brent +3.58% to $99.58 May 26 on the US strikes; ~-14% MoM net tail-premium de-pricing) and USD/INR gave back its firming to ₹95.68 (rupee weaker) — net, the import-bill / under-recovery envelope is marginally better than the May peak but $99 Brent + ₹95.68 still sits above the ~$85-90 break-even ceiling. Hardeep Puri's ~₹1,000 cr/day under-recovery quantification (May 13) remains the operative fiscal framing; the cumulative ₹7.5/L is the inflation-transmission channel feeding core CPI. **Watch**: whether the pause holds or a fifth hike resumes the cadence. (NOTE: operative Brent ~$99, NOT the yfinance -6.8%/$92.78 roll artifact.)

recent_signals.headline: **FOURTH OMC HIKE +₹2.61-2.71/L MAY 25 — LARGEST OF THE SEQUENCE; PATTERN-BREAK TO A COST-RECOVERY CADENCE.** OMCs (IOC/BPCL/HPCL, ~90% of retail) raised petrol+diesel by ₹2.61-2.71/litre Monday May 25 — the fourth increase in under two weeks and the LARGEST single hike of the cascade (May 15 +₹3; May 19 +~90p; May 23 +~87-91p; May 25 +₹2.61-2.71), cumulative ~₹7.5/L since revisions resumed May 15. Prices: Mumbai petrol ₹111.21 / diesel ₹97.83; Kolkata petrol ₹113.51 / diesel ₹99.82; Chennai petrol ₹107.77 (India TV News, Goodreturns May 25). **The mechanism / regime read**: a large Monday hike landing on a US/UK market holiday, the day before the RBI swap auction and the Quad, materially revises the prior 'Saturday-only, calibrated-to-political-tolerance' thesis. OMC pass-through is now tracking cost recovery / refining-margin pressure and a weak rupee more than a political-tolerance calendar — the seal is fully broken and the cadence is now economics-led. **Counter-current**: this landed on a deal-relief day (Brent slid below $100, USD/INR firmed to ₹95.22), which modestly eases the import-bill/under-recovery envelope at the margin — but $100 Brent + ₹95.22 still sits above the ~$85-90 break-even ceiling, so marketing margins stay structurally compressed. That the LARGEST hike came on a relief day is itself the cleanest confirmation the pass-through is cost-recovery-driven, not opportunistic. Hardeep Puri's ~₹1,000 cr/day under-recovery quantification (May 13) remains operative; the cumulative ₹7.5/L is the inflation-transmission channel feeding core CPI and compressing RBI optionality. The April 27 fuel-pass-through trigger stays `active_fired`, firing harder.

recent_signals.headline: **OMC PASS-THROUGH ACTIVATED — TWO ~90 PAISE PETROL/DIESEL HIKES IN A WEEK; APRIL 27 FUEL-PASS-THROUGH TRIGGER FIRES INSIDE 30-DAY WINDOW.** The Modi government chose to break the political seal — pre-2024-election it deferred price hikes for 5 quarters; choosing TWO hikes in a week now signals fiscal patience is exhausted. **Mechanism**: India imports ~85% of crude; sustained Brent $109-111 + USD/INR ₹96 + the May 1 weekly-reserves drawdown of $7.79B forced OMCs to either continue absorbing the import-bill shock (IOC/BPCL/HPCL Q4 margin destruction, 3 weeks of stock-price punishment of OMCs has been pricing this) or pass it through to consumers. **The government chose passthrough — margin-protective for OMCs but politically explosive.** Pre-election the deferral was political; the pass-through now is policy. **Follow-on**: 90 paise increase = ~0.85% inflation contribution if sustained; food/transport inflation will follow with 2-3 week lag.

recent_signals.headline: The OMC margin hole is materially larger than any published official figure and no relief is coming. Brent settled $88.10 with pump prices never cut. The last official numbers — Q1 FY27 under-recoveries ~Rs1.88 lakh cr and actual OMC losses ~Rs74,781 cr — were framed by Petroleum Minister Puri on 2 July **around crude at ~$70**, and PREDATE the July spike; his '2-3 months away' timeline for any price cut was built on a price that no longer exists. No excise cut, no OMC compensation package, no SPR release announced 17-19 Jul, no GST Council meeting, no stimulus. Given Rs1 lakh cr of excise revenue already sacrificed, the absence of action may reflect fiscal CAPACITY rather than choice. **Expect this to surface as a FISCAL story before a pump-price story.** Adjacent and under-priced: India's LPG import channel is Hormuz-dependent and running 50% below pre-conflict volumes, which hits the subsidised cooking-gas book directly. CONFIRMED (the non-action).
